candidates.question: A SQL Server 2022 service has validated that @detail contains the JSON object shown below. Its response must contain a nested detail object, not a JSON string containing the document text. Which replacement expression preserves that structure?
candidates.explanation: Project JSON_QUERY(@detail) so FOR JSON embeds the existing object.
candidates.deepExplanation: The object is already valid JSON. The remaining issue is preserving its structural meaning across serialization, not removing escaping from arbitrary unvalidated text.

whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.a: A plain text expression is not marked as a JSON fragment; the cited JSON_QUERY guidance requires wrapping preformatted JSON for FOR JSON output.
whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.b: This extracts only the scalar code, losing the required object and units field.
whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.d: This extracts only the scalar units value as text, not the full structured detail object.

candidates.subskill: Write queries that include JSON functions, such as JSON\_OBJECT, JSON\_ARRAY, JSON\_ARRAYAGG, JSON\_CONTAINS, OPENJSON, and JSON\_VALUE
candidates.codeSnippet:
DECLARE @detail nvarchar(max) = N'{"code":"N8","units":3}';
SELECT /* expression */ AS detail FOR JSON PATH;
